title: metadata-protocol: the /meta door's 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT carries details.candidates, as /automation and /actions do (ADR-0150 D5)
body:
domain:server#4 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzi1tLRTEYwYGtbNCyk

Filed by seat 4 from the epic seat's text (`epic:#31527#1`, red-line read 6766975502 on PR #32197). ⛔ Not a claim.
Ruling-ref: 6766975502 (epic: a new server card, p2, a child of #31527).

④ coordination card: a child of the ADR-0150 epic #31527.

**Epic:** ADR-0150 (#31527). **Lane:** `domain:server` (metadata-protocol, rest). **Reader:** the server seat that claims it.
**Found by** #31695 / PR #32197 (the client SDK's optional `namespace`): the SDK can read a `409`'s holders structurally on `/automation` and `/actions` (`error.details.candidates`), but not on `/meta`.

### The gap

The `/meta` by-name read answers `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` when an address names no one item (a bare name two packages hold, or a qualifier whose package holds no item of the name while another holder does). Today its holders appear in the message only: `thrownAnswerOf` (`packages/types/src/actions-door-answer.ts`) carries no `details.candidates` for this door, so an SDK caller (`client.meta.getItem`) cannot retry with the intended holder without parsing prose. `/automation` and `/actions` already answer `details.candidates` as a `PackageScopedHolder` list (`{ kind: 'package', packageId }` or `{ kind: 'environment' }`).

### Do

1. The `/meta` door's `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` carries `details.candidates`: the same `PackageScopedHolder` list, in the same shape as `/automation` and `/actions`. The message stays as it is.
2. **Pins**, one per `/meta` read form, each asserting `status` 409, `error.code`, and `details.candidates` deep-equal to the holders:
   - bare `GET /meta/:type/:name`
   - exact qualifier `?package=`
   - qualified `/meta/:type/:ns/:name`
   - `/meta/:type/_env/:name`
   Ablating the candidates carry turns them red.
3. Once it lands, `client.meta.getItem`'s doc and changeset (PR #32197) say the rejection carries no `details.candidates`. That note becomes false, so the PR that lands this updates it, or names the follow-up.

**Clause-②:** `yes (widening)`: an additive `details` member on an existing refusal. No answer that succeeds changes.
**Dedupe** (open and closed: `candidates`, `409`, `meta`): none for this. #31691 (closed) built the doors' namespace segment and the `/automation` candidates; #32199 is the `/layers` exact-qualifier judgment, another defect.
**Business reason:** when two installed packages ship an item under one name, a console or an integration reading it through the SDK has to choose the holder. Without the list it can only show the raw message.
**Epic red-line review before landing.**
